note: Triennial election of the Dungannon rural district councillors, 1933. 'There will be no contest in any of the district electoral divisions of Dungannon Rural Council' (Ulster Herald, 22 April 1933, p. 5); the nominations list is printed in the Irish News, 19 April 1933, p. 6 (one name for each division; read on the page image, council-audit, Nov 2026). Eleven of the nineteen divisions are recorded by the meeting method (7 Nov 2026): each member is the 1930 return for the division and sat at the new council's statutory meeting on Tuesday 6 June 1933 (Mid-Ulster Mail, 10 June 1933, p. 5). Not recorded: Altmore, Clonavaddy, Crossdernott, Donaghmore and Granville (the 1930 members are not named at the meeting); Minterburn (Mr. M. Busby, the member from 1936, sits, not the 1930 member); Castlecaulfield (Colonel Howard and Mr. M. D. Brown both sit, and a Mr. M. Brown was co-opted); and Anahoe (both Mr. T. D. Givans and Mr. T. J. Cuddy appear). No poll was held; Tyrone's polling day was Wednesday 31 May 1933. division inferred from the 4 June 1930 return (James Watt); the Mid-Ulster Mail, 10 June 1933, p. 5 names the member as returned, sitting at the new council's first meeting, where Mrs. Brown, Mr. M. Brown and Mr. William Moffatt were co-opted. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Citation completed from the page image of Irish News, 19 April 1933, p. 6 (council-audit, Nov 2026): the nominations list is now cited. Corrected from the page image of the Irish News, 19 April 1933, p. 6 (w8-review, Nov 2026): the Bernagh nominee returned unopposed is Mr. James Webb, as the list prints him (was J. Watt, inferred from the 1930 member); the J. Watt of the 1933 council is R. J. Watt, whom the same list returns for Crossdernott. Reverted (research-K1, MG-96, owner-approved 13 Nov 2026): the Bernagh nominee is James Watt of Dunseark, who held the division in 1927 and 1930. The Bernagh nominations print "J. Watt" (Northern Whig, 25 March 1933, p. 6; Frontier Sentinel, 1 April 1933, p. 6), and James Watt of Dunseark is named in the Armagh Guardian, 20 March 1931, p. 8; no James Webb appears in Dungannon in 1920-50, so the Irish News's "Mr. James Webb" is a misprint for him.
